questions.question: The fish is above the duck. Where is the duck?
questions.explain: If the fish is above the duck, then the duck is below the fish. Above and below are opposites, so it is easy to pick the wrong one.

questions.question: The pen is to the left of the book. Where is the book?
questions.explain: If the pen is to the left of the book, the book must be to the right of the pen. Left and right are easy to swap by mistake.

questions.question: The bird is below the cloud. Where is the cloud?
questions.explain: If the bird is below the cloud, the cloud is above the bird. Remember: below and above are opposite words.

questions.question: Mia puts her shoes under her bed. Where are Mia's shoes?
questions.explain: Under means below, so the shoes are below the bed. Picking above would be the opposite, which is the trap here.

questions.question: Tom sits to the left of Anna at lunch. Where does Anna sit?
questions.explain: If Tom is to the left of Anna, then Anna is to the right of Tom. Left and right swap easily, so watch for that.

questions.question: Nina puts a cookie on top of a cup. Where is the cookie?
questions.explain: On top of means above, so the cookie is above the cup. Below would be the opposite, which is the trap.

questions.question: A hat is above a cup. A cup is on a table. Where is the table in relation to the hat?
questions.explain: The hat is above the cup and the cup is on the table, so the table is below the hat. The trap is picking above, which is the opposite.

questions.question: A boy stands to the left of a girl. The girl stands to the left of a cat. Who is on the right?
questions.explain: The order from left to right is boy, girl, cat. So the cat is on the right. It is easy to mix up the boy and the cat.

questions.question: A ball is to the right of a book. A book is to the right of a pen. Where is the pen in relation to the ball?
questions.explain: The order from left to right is pen, book, ball. So the pen is to the left of the ball. Left and right are easy to swap.

questions.question: A kid says: The ball is to the right of the tree. But the ball is to the left of the tree. What did the kid get wrong?
options: He put the ball in a tree
He said the tree is the ball
questions.explain: The kid said right but it should be left. That is swapping left and right. Above and below are a different pair of words.

questions.question: The sun is above the tree. Where is the tree?
questions.explain: If the sun is above the tree, then the tree is below the sun. A common mix-up is saying above when it should be below.

questions.question: The pencil is to the right of the eraser. Where is the eraser?
questions.explain: If the pencil is to the right of the eraser, then the eraser is to the left of the pencil. A common mix-up is swapping left and right.

questions.question: At snack time, Sam puts the cookie on top of the plate. Where is the plate?
questions.explain: If the cookie is on top of the plate, then the plate is below the cookie. A common mix-up is saying above when it should be below.

questions.question: At the table, a fork sits to the left of a plate. Where is the plate?
questions.explain: If the fork is to the left of the plate, then the plate is to the right of the fork. A common mix-up is swapping left and right.
